maria (sec): Heads up — our on-call ran the backup-agent update to 2.4.1 and the runtime scan flagged a possible vuln: the agent writes a short-lived plaintext header to /tmp during multipart uploads. Potential CVE?
jon (infra): omg, where did that header come from? is it the retry logic for the multipart assembler?
kevin (sre): saw noisy alerts from objectstore GC last night, but didn’t connect to agent update. link to last night's logs: https://logs.internal/xyz (redacted)
olivia (prodsec): timeline: patch rolled at 02:10, GC job ran 02:30, object re-upload at 02:31. The header included an `Encryption-Context` string and a CMK id. Not the key material but still sensitive metadata.
maria (sec): tagging @jon for RBAC question: backup-service-account currently has kms:Decrypt+Encrypt. We should flip to Encrypt-only for the upload path and require ephemeral grants for Decrypt. Thoughts? :thinking:
jon (infra): agree on least privilege. Backup coordinator can Encrypt; restore path should request a short-lived grant (kms:Decrypt) via admin service account that we rotate session creds on.
kevin (sre): operationally, ephemeral grants add latency during restores; we should measure impact. Also need audit logs to surface CMK id + encryption context so we can trace who requested decrypts.
backup-bot: [backup-svc] completed upload job job-783: 02:31:12 status=success size=14GB cmk=arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:alias/backup-main
maria (sec): backup-bot log proves metadata was emitted. Noting two concerns: 1) storing encryption context in plaintext /tmp on nodes (file perms too open), and 2) missing structured audit fields in our enqueue logs.
jon (infra): quick mitigation: patch the agent to write tmp files under mode 0600 and rotate location to ramfs, and scrub file immediately after multipart completes. I'll open PR.
olivia (prodsec): longer term: change logging schema so that the audit pipeline includes `cmk_alias`, `encryption_context_hash` (not raw), and `operation_id`. We should avoid sending raw context strings to slow log stores.
kevin (sre): can we detect previously leaked contexts by scanning S3 object metadata for header presence? I can run a bucket scan script if you give me list of high-risk buckets.
maria (sec): yes, please scan prod-backups and tenant-archive buckets. If found, we need to rotate CMKs for affected objects and trigger tenant notifications per policy.
jon (infra): PR: https://git.internal/r/backup-agent/pull/452 — implements 0600, ramfs write, immediate unlink, plus flag `--no-store-context` to avoid writing context to disk.
kevin (sre): will push a one-off job to scan buckets once PR is rolled. Estimate ~2 hours for first pass.
olivia (prodsec): policy change proposal: backup-service-account role gets `kms:Encrypt` only. Restore service will be `restore-service` with temporary `kms:Decrypt` via `kms:Grant` or STS-assumed-role. Also we add an alert on any object metadata containing raw `Encryption-Context` key.
maria (sec): triage notes for incident record: severity=medium, vector=backup-agent tmp file, impact=metadata exposure (no keys), remediation=agent patch + RBAC change + audit schema migration + bucket scan + CMK rotation if needed. Assign to jon/kevin.
jon (infra): rolling patch to canary tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Will gate on a successful canary scan of 50 objects.
kevin (sre): will coordinate bucket scan after canary. I’ll post results in this thread.
maria (sec): thanks all. we should also add a unit test in agent that ensures no plaintext context is persisted. Example snippet for test:
```
assert not os.path.exists('/tmp/backup_context_*')
```
olivia (prodsec): also file a compliance ticket to update audit retention for the new structured fields.
jon (infra): ack. i'll update infra-iam.yaml to remove kms:Decrypt for backup-svc and add role assumption docs.
kevin (sre): quick status — canary patch queued, bucket-scan job scheduled at 06:00 UTC. will report back. :white_check_mark:
